headline: British Army Officer Recruitment 2026: Sandhurst Entry Guide
metaDescription: British Army officer recruitment 2026: age 18-29, 42-week Sandhurst course, nationality rules, AOSB selection, fitness standards and starting pay explained.

sections.content:
British Army officers lead soldiers from day one — managing teams, planning operations and taking responsibility for training, discipline and welfare. Every officer, Regular or Reserve, completes initial officer training at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst, which runs three intakes each year in January, May and September.

The 42-week Commissioning Course is deliberately intense: leadership development, tactics, academic military studies, physical conditioning and adventurous training are packed into under a year. It concludes with the Sovereign's Parade, after which cadets commission as Second Lieutenants and move on to specialist training with their chosen regiment or corps.
sections.title: The Officer Role and Sandhurst Training

sections.content:
Regular officer candidates must be aged 18 to 29 when training begins. Soldier entry is broader — you can apply from 16 with enlistment before your 36th birthday — while reserve officer entry extends to 48. Anyone under 18 needs written parental consent.

On nationality, you must normally be a British citizen, an Irish citizen, or a Commonwealth citizen with the legal right to live and work in the UK. There are no mandatory formal qualifications for many roles, though technical trades ask for GCSEs or equivalents in English and maths. What the Army is really screening for at this stage is leadership potential, motivation and the values expected of an officer.
sections.title: Eligibility: Age, Nationality and Education

sections.content:
After the online application and medical questionnaires, candidates face the Army Officer Selection Board — first a briefing, then the main board. AOSB assesses leadership, teamwork, problem-solving and physical robustness through command tasks, interviews, written exercises and fitness assessments spread over several days.

The fitness component centres on the multistage bleep test: male candidates generally need level 10.2 and female candidates level 8.1, alongside strength and endurance events. Preparation matters — arrive already fit, because the board is designed to find your limits. From application to starting training, expect a timeline of at least six months.
sections.title: AOSB Selection and Fitness Assessment

sections.content:
Newly commissioned officers earn a starting salary of around £35,925, rising with rank, seniority and specialist qualifications — infantry officers, for example, are advertised in the £35,925 to £42,948 band. Officers also receive subsidised accommodation, medical and dental care, and a non-contributory pension that compares well with civilian schemes.

Career progression runs from Second Lieutenant through Lieutenant, Captain, Major and beyond, with command appointments, staff roles and sponsored postgraduate education along the way. Many officers later convert that leadership and management experience into strong civilian careers, which is part of the long-term value of a commission.
